PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 19, audited at commit 50a628a (HEAD of the main checkout, tree 90be71d2...). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. Eleven files, 2750 insertions, two of them the committed handoff and prototype. VERDICT: PASS, with one discrepancy between the record and the code that should be reconciled before this sprint closes -- see finding 1. It is not a code fix and I explain below why I did not make it a condition. R11 WAS THE CRITERION MOST AT RISK, and it held. At Sprint 18's gate I predicted that the sprint which needed styled, animated, staggered paragraphs would be the one to reach for a markdown renderer. This is that sprint. It did not. Grepped app/, lib/ and package.json for dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, react-markdown, remark, rehype, "marked" and markdown-it. One hit in the entire repository: the comment in display.ts telling people not to. package.json is untouched by this sprint -- no dependency was added at all. The paragraphs are still horoscopeParagraphs()'s newline split mapped to

{paragraph}

, now with a class and an inline animationDelay, which changes nothing about the escaping. The convenient path stayed the safe path, which is what README's standing note was written to achieve, and it is the first time that note has been tested against the exact temptation it names. R12 also held: isSafeExternalUrl still gates event.sourceUrl at page.tsx:282, and its four tests including the javascript: rejection are intact. R3 -- fonts. MET, and I chased the one hit that looked like a failure so nobody else has to. Grepping .next for fonts.googleapis returns exactly one file: a server-side source map. The matched string is Dev Team's own comment, "no runtime request to fonts.googleapis.com or any other host". Not a request, not in .next/static, not in any non-map file. Then the decisive check: served the built app and grepped the delivered HTML for any absolute URL -- zero external hosts of any kind. 25 self-hosted .woff2 assets. The project's zero-outbound-runtime-requests property survives a typography-heavy design sprint, which is the sprint most likely to cost it. Requirements coverage: R1 MET. Colours are oklch() throughout -- 16 declarations in globals.css, 9 in the module, the rest via custom properties -- and grepping both files for hex and rgb() returns nothing. Nothing was converted. R2 MET. The prefers-color-scheme block is gone, not overridden; the only occurrence of that string in app/ is a comment recording its removal. body's margin is gone too. R3 MET. See above. R4 MET. Grepped app/ and lib/ for ELEM, helio, moonLon, lonAt, keplerian, meanAnom, eccentric, perihelion, semimajor and obliquity: one hit, a comment in constellation.ts saying none of it is there. The file imports PlanetPosition and Aspect as types and computeMoonPhase as the only function, and computes screen coordinates. R5 MET. computeMoonPhaseGeometry derives its path from computeMoonPhase(positions)'s elongation -- lib/ephemeris's own value, not a local recomputation. R6 MET by the honest route. statusLabel is pending ? "writing" : hasHoroscope ? "written" : "not read yet" -- three states, no fourth. The submit phase is not faked on a timer, which is what R6 actually asked for when it said ship only `writing` if the two cannot be distinguished. R7 MET in structure, not in letter -- see finding 1. page.tsx has no "use client"; exactly one client component exists; hasHoroscope is computed server-side and never duplicated client-side. R8 MET in implementation. The rise class and its animationDelay are applied only when justWrote is true, which can only become true by observing a pending -> not-pending transition with no errorMessage. A page load of an already-written reading starts with pending false and justWrote false, so the animation cannot replay, and a failed regenerate is explicitly excluded so the unchanged paragraphs do not re-animate. See note 2 for what no gate here can confirm about it. R9 MET, and more strictly than Sprint 13 did it. I parsed both stylesheets and checked every animation and transition declaration for whether it sits inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference block. Every one does. The only line outside is `animation: none !important` inside the reduce block, which is a disable rather than an animation. That is true opt-in rather than Sprint 13's opt-out override, and the module's own comment records the change deliberately. R10 MET. generateReadingHoroscope is unchanged and still the only trigger; nothing generates on load. R11 MET. See above. R12 MET. See above. R13 MET. git diff over README.md is empty -- the standing note is untouched. R14 MET. Grepped both stylesheets for @media: the only ones are prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme's absence. No width breakpoint crept in. Verified by execution: - lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 179 tests across 18 files, 17 new. - next build exits 0; route table unchanged. - Built with probe values for OPENAI_API_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and grepped the whole .next output: both absent. - Served the built app: zero external hosts in the delivered HTML. Worth crediting specifically: constellation.ts says it was recovered from commit 9b132e3 rather than re-derived. That is the post-fix Sprint 13 commit, not 2fb6062, and it matters -- I checked, and both fixes I required there came across with it. The three handoff body-mark colours (0.88 0.06 85, 0.80 0.05 145, 0.74 0.11 25) are present, and the dead ASPECT_MAX_ORB table is still absent. Recovering audited work from the audited commit rather than the first one is a small decision that quietly prevented re-litigating two rounds of Sprint 13. FINDING 1 -- the record and the code disagree about R7, and the code is right. R7 says, in the requirement and again in the acceptance criterion: "Exactly one piece of client state -- the pending flag" and "holds only the pending flag". ReadingPanel holds three: useFormStatus's pending, plus prevPending and justWrote. R8 is why. "Only on first appearance after generation" cannot be derived from pending alone -- something has to remember that a pending -> not-pending transition happened in this instance. R7 as written and R8 as written cannot both be satisfied, which is the same shape as Sprint 14's R1/R8 contradiction, and it was resolved there by amending the criterion with a dated note owning it. The code handles it well. The extra state is documented at length, neither variable duplicates server-owned data, and the comment correctly identifies the pattern as React's documented "adjusting state when a prop changes" -- comparing against a previous-value state variable and conditionally calling setState during render -- and explains why an effect or a ref would each be worse. It also records that the deviation was decided with the user. I chose PASS rather than CONDITIONAL, and the reasoning belongs on the record so it can be overruled. Every requirement's purpose is met; the only thing unmet is a sentence describing an implementation detail that another requirement makes impossible. The user has already adjudicated the substance. And the remedy is an amendment to the sprint file, which is Master Controller's to write -- a CONDITIONAL would route this sprint back to dev_build for work Dev Team cannot do. What I am asking for is that the deviation be recorded in the sprint file the way Sprint 13's client-UUID deviation and Sprint 14's R1 contradiction both were, before this sprint closes. A deviation living only in a code comment is one refactor away from looking like a mistake. Notes: 2. Whether the rise animation ever actually runs is unverifiable by any gate in this process, and it fails safe rather than dangerously. justWrote can only become true if the component instance survives the server action's redirect -- the action redirects to /reading/, the same route it was already on, so React would normally preserve the instance and the pending -> not-pending transition is observed. If it remounts instead, justWrote starts false and the paragraphs simply appear without animating. That is the correct failure direction: R8's prohibition holds either way, and the worst case is a missing flourish rather than a stored reading pretending to be freshly written. I have no browser and neither does GroundTruth. Add it to the user's browser check explicitly: press "Read the chart" and confirm the paragraphs rise in, then reload and confirm they do not. Those two observations together are the only proof R8 works, and the sprint file's "Verified by the user, not by a gate" section is the right home for them. 3. The one fonts.googleapis hit in .next is a source map containing Dev Team's own comment about not calling Google Fonts. Recording it because the next person to run that grep will find it and it looks alarming for about ten seconds. 4. Carried and unchanged from earlier sprints, all still true and none of them this sprint's business: readingId is still interpolated unencoded into the redirect path (re-checked, still cannot escape the origin), searchParams.error is still reflected as escaped text, and display.ts's isSafeExternalUrl comment still understates the threat it defends against relative to README's now-authoritative version. On what this gate cannot tell anyone: the sprint file is right that visual fidelity is unverifiable here, and it is right to name a person who owns it rather than leaving it implied. I can confirm this page serves, is safe, carries the specified structure, and introduces no external dependency. I cannot confirm it looks like the design. On a high-fidelity design sprint that is most of what matters, and the record should not read as though a PASS covered it. Cleared to ship at 50a628a. GroundTruth's third criterion -- the Sprint 18 XSS payloads still rendering escaped after a full visual rewrite of the page that renders them -- is the one worth running first.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 19, round 2. Audited at commit 50a628a -- unchanged from round 1.
HEAD's tree is 90be71d2..., byte-identical to the tree my round-1 PASS recorded, so no
code moved. The sprint file changed, which is the entire reason there is a round 2 and
the reason this re-stamps the file hash so /sprint-dev-done can proceed.

VERDICT: PASS.

R7's REQUIREMENT IS NOW RECORDED PROPERLY, which is what I asked for.

The amendment states that "exactly one piece of client state" was unsatisfiable
alongside R8, names the accepted implementation and its three state variables, records
that none duplicates server-owned data, identifies the React pattern used and why an
effect or a ref would be worse, and notes the substance was adjudicated with the user
before it was built. It also owns the contradiction as the author's own and observes
it is the second of its shape after Sprint 14's R1/R8. That is a better amendment than
I asked for -- I asked for the deviation to be recorded, and what landed also explains
why the original wording could not have been met, which is the part that stops someone
"restoring" the single-state version later.

Round 1's coverage of R1 through R14 stands unchanged. The tree is identical, so I did
not re-run lint, typecheck, test or build -- they exited 0 against these exact bytes
one round ago and would tell me the same thing again. R11 and R12, the two criteria
most at risk, are properties of code that has not moved.

ONE PIECE OF THE RECONCILIATION IS MISSING, and it is the half I actually audit
against.

The requirement at line 44 is amended. The acceptance criterion at line 98 is not:

  - R7: `page.tsx` has no `"use client"`. Exactly one client component exists, and it
    holds only the pending flag.

"holds only the pending flag" is still there, still describes something the accepted
implementation deliberately does not do, and sits under a heading that reads
"QA1 -- static, from the diff". That section is the list a gate is pointed at. A future
QA1 reading the criteria and not the requirement would fail a correct diff on it, and
the requirement's own amendment is fifty lines away with nothing linking them.

I am passing rather than sending this back, for the same reasons as round 1: the code
is right and unchanged, the substance is adjudicated, and editing a sprint file is
Master Controller's to do rather than Dev Team's, so a CONDITIONAL would route this to
the wrong owner for a one-line edit. It should still be done before the sprint closes
-- strike the clause, or append "see R7's amendment" to it. Either takes a moment.

WORTH SAYING BECAUSE IT HAS NOW HAPPENED TWICE, in the same way. Sprint 4 amended R8's
requirement and left R8's criterion contradicting it, and I flagged that the criterion
would lead the next reader to fail a correct diff. This is the same omission with a
different number on it. Both times the amendment was thoughtful and the criterion was
simply forgotten, which suggests it is procedural rather than careless: an amendment
naturally gets written where the requirement is, and the criteria section is a separate
list further down the same file. Whoever writes the next amendment is better served by
a habit than by care -- when a requirement changes, grep the criteria section for its
number before saving. It costs nothing and it is the second time it would have helped.

Notes carried from round 1, all unchanged and none of them blocking:
1. Whether the rise animation ever runs is unverifiable by any gate here and fails
   safe. It depends on the component instance surviving the server action's same-route
   redirect. Add it to the user's browser check explicitly: press "Read the chart" and
   confirm the paragraphs rise in, then reload and confirm they do not. Those two
   observations together are the only proof R8 works, and neither I nor GroundTruth can
   make them.
2. The single fonts.googleapis hit in .next is a server source map containing Dev
   Team's own comment about not calling Google Fonts. Not a request, not in
   .next/static, and the delivered HTML contains no external host at all.
3. readingId is still interpolated unencoded into the redirect path (cannot escape the
   origin), searchParams.error is still reflected as escaped text, and display.ts's
   isSafeExternalUrl comment still understates the threat relative to README's
   authoritative version.

And the thing this gate still cannot tell anyone, restated because a second PASS should
not quietly imply otherwise: I can confirm this page serves, is safe, carries the
specified structure and introduces no external dependency. I cannot confirm it looks
like the design. The sprint file names a person who owns that check before the close,
which is the right answer, and it has not happened yet.

Cleared to ship at 50a628a.
